project.overview.description: No parameters: the overview of the open project.

binder.read_tree.description: Which part of the binder to read.

root.description: A node id to start from: root (the default), manuscript, research, or any id.

depth.description: Levels below the start node to include: 1 to 3.

include.description: Per node: word counts (default), the synopsis, or nothing extra.

doc.read.description: Which document to read, and how much of it.

doc.description: The document: a title, or an id. An ambiguous title lists its candidates.

range.description: A character range in the body projection, from and to, 0-indexed. Omit for the whole body.

response_format.description: 'detailed' returns the text. 'concise' returns structure and a lead.

notes.read.description: Which document, and which inspector fields.

doc.description: The document: a title, or an id. An ambiguous title lists its candidates.

fields.description: The fields to read: a list of synopsis, notes and keywords, or "all" (the default).

anyOf.description: A list of the fields to read, in the order given.

meta.set.description: The documents or folders to change, and the metadata to set on each.

targets.description: Documents or folders to change: a title or an id each. At most 50 per call.

items.description: One target: a title, or an id.

status.description: A status id from the project vocabulary.

label.description: A label id from the project vocabulary.

keywords_add.description: Keywords to add to each target. A keyword already present is left as it is.

keywords_remove.description: Keywords to remove from each target. A keyword not present is ignored.

notes.append.description: The document, and the text to append to its notes.

doc.description: The document: a title, or an id. An ambiguous title lists its candidates.

text.description: The text to append, at most 2000 characters.

synopsis.fill.description: The documents to draft synopses for, and how.

docs.description: Documents to draft a synopsis for: a title or an id each, at most 20 per call.

items.description: One document: a title, or an id.

source.description: What to draft from: the text, the notes, or both.

max_words.description: The longest synopsis to draft, in words.

scene.draft.description: The document to draft into, the brief, and how to write.

doc.description: The document: a title, or an id.

target_words.description: The length to aim for, in words.

mode.description: draft replaces an empty body; continue appends; rewrite_selection replaces the anchored range.

selection.description: A range in the body projection, captured from the editor selection.

to.description: End offset, exclusive. Greater than from.

exact.description: The text between from and to, 1 to 2000 characters.

capturedRevision.description: The document revision when the anchor was captured.

include_forward_outline.description: Include the synopses of the later scenes in the drafting context. Off by default; turn it on when the draft must lead into what follows.

binder.restructure.description: The batch of binder operations, applied in order.

ops.description: Operations, in order: at most 30. Each is a create, a move or a rename, and names existing node ids only.

oneOf.description: Create a folder or a document. A document goes in a chapter, not the manuscript.

parent.description: The id of the folder or root that will hold the new node.

type.description: Whether the new node is a folder or a document.

title.description: The title of the new node.

oneOf.description: Move an existing node under a new parent, at a position among its siblings.

node.description: The id of the node to move.

newParent.description: The id of the folder or root it moves under.

index.description: The position among the new parent’s children, from 0.

oneOf.description: Change the title of an existing node.

node.description: The id of the node to rename.

continuity.scan.description: Which documents to check, and for what.

scope.description: Documents to check: titles or ids, at most 20. Omit for the whole manuscript, which must hold 20 documents or fewer.

items.description: One document: a title, or an id.

aspects.description: What to check: timeline, characters, props or custom. Omit for all of them.

export.compile.description: What to compile, and in what format.

selection.description: The node to compile. The manuscript compiles the whole manuscript; any other node compiles a part. Leave it out when a recipe names the nodes.

root.description: A node id or a title: manuscript, or any node under it.

includeSubtrees.description: Include everything under the root. Defaults to true, so a chapter exports with its scenes. False names the node alone.

template.description: An export template id. Omit for the default template. A prompt pack names its vendor template here, unless the recipe does.

recipeName.description: A saved export recipe, by name. It supplies the title page, contents, author, character limit and template, and without a selection, its nodes.

query.description: A case-insensitive substring to match against names, aliases and descriptions.

type.description: Only entries of this type, or all.

includePolicy.description: Only entries with this policy, or all.

id.description: An exact entry id. Returns that entry with its full description.

limit.description: How many entries to return: 1 to 100.

codex.write.description: The codex entries to create or update, as one batch.

entries.description: Entries to create or update: at most 20 per call. Each is validated before any of them is written.

items.description: One codex entry: a create, or an update of an existing entry by id.

action.description: create makes a new entry; update changes one named by id.

id.description: The id of the entry to update. Required for an update; not set on a create.

name.description: The entry name, at most 120 characters. Required on a create.

aliases.description: Other names the entry is found by, at most 10.

description.description: The entry description. At most 2000 characters; a longer one fails the batch with a proposed truncation.

includePolicy.description: When the entry is included in the context of a generation call.

caseSensitive.description: Whether the name and aliases match case-sensitively.

exclude.description: Phrases in which matches are ignored, at most 20.

attachTo.description: Binder node ids to attach the entry to.

detachFrom.description: Binder node ids to detach the entry from.

visualRefs.description: The image asset ids the entry's visual references are, at most 10: images already in this project, by id. An update replaces the list.

agent.plan.description: A plan: an ordered list of tool calls, each with the effect it expects.

steps.description: The steps, in order. At least one.

items.description: One step: a tool call and the effect it should have.

tool.description: The tool this step calls, by name.

params.description: The tool’s params. The tool checks them when the plan is preflighted.

expect.description: The effect the step should have, in words, shown on the card.

doc.import.description: The document to import, stored exactly as given, with its metadata.

parent.description: The chapter or folder that holds the document: a title or an id.

body.description: The body, as markdown. Stored exactly as given: no paraphrase, no trimming.

keywords.description: Keywords, at most 32, each at most 64 characters.

status.description: A status id from the project vocabulary.

label.description: A label id from the project vocabulary.

codex.import.description: The codex entries to import, as one batch. Each is created as the writer’s own canon and attached to the document it cites.

entries.description: Entries to import: at most 20 per call, create-only. Each is validated before any of them is written.

items.description: One imported codex entry: a new entry, attached to the document its text came from.

name.description: The entry name, at most 120 characters. Required, and unique across the codex.

aliases.description: Other names the entry is found by, at most 10. None may equal another entry's name or alias.

description.description: The entry description. At most 2000 characters.

includePolicy.description: When the entry is included in the context of a generation call.

caseSensitive.description: Whether the name and aliases match case-sensitively.

exclude.description: Phrases in which matches are ignored, at most 20.

attachTo.description: The one document the entry is attached to and cites: the document its full text was imported into. Required.

coherence.scan.description: Scope and checks for a deterministic coherence scan.

scope.description: Which documents to read. "doc" reads one document (docIds holds exactly its id); "changed" reads documents edited since their last review; "full" reads the manuscript.

docIds.description: For mode "doc" only: the one document id to read.

checks.description: The deterministic checks to run. Omit for all eight.

coherence.review.description: Scope, categories and cap for a model-judged review.

scope.description: Which documents to read. "doc" reads one document (docIds holds exactly its id); "changed" reads documents edited since their last review; "full" reads the manuscript.

docIds.description: For mode "doc" only: the one document id to read.

categories.description: The categories to review. Omit for all five.

maxFindings.description: The most findings to record. Defaults to 50; capped at 200.

coherence.setFindingStatus.description: The finding and the status to set.

findingId.description: The finding id, from a run report or the inbox.

status.description: Only "fixed" is settable by the agent.

query.description: A word or phrase to match against tool names, descriptions and topics. Empty lists the first matches.

server.description: Limit the search to one external server, by its key (the s_ form shown in the server list). Native tools are then left out.

risk.description: Limit to 'read' tools (run without a confirmation) or 'write' tools (each call asks the user).

limit.description: How many matches to return, from 1 to 20. Defaults to 8.

shots.derive.description: The scene to derive shots from, and how.

doc.description: The screenplay scene: a document id, resolved from its title first.

granularity.description: key-shots covers the scene with the shots that carry it; full-coverage covers every line of dialogue and action.

styleNote.description: A shot style to follow, e.g. handheld and tight, passed to the model with the scene.

shots.annotate.description: The shots to change and what to set on them.

shots.description: The shot ids to change, each named once.

items.description: A shot id, read from binder.read_tree.

image.description: An image already in assets/, by its id.

assetId.description: The asset id the import returned.

spec.description: The camera fields to set. Any subset.

lens.description: The lens, as free text, e.g. 35mm anamorphic.

prompt.draft.description: The shots to draft, the vendor template and the creative direction.

shots.description: The storyboard shot ids to draft, in any order. At most 30 per call; split a longer list.

vendor.description: The vendor template id, for example runway-gen4.

instruction.description: Creative direction applied to every shot in the call.

prompt.variant.description: The shot, the vendor template and the part of the prompt to vary.

vendor.description: The vendor template id, for example runway-gen4.

variation.description: The part of the prompt to vary: camera, lighting, style or audio.

dialogue.draft.description: The container, the brief, and where the draft goes.

doc.description: The dialogue container, by title or id.

instruction.description: The creative brief for the beats.

fromBeats.description: Knot or stitch ids to continue from. The draft goes after the last one. Omit to append at the end.

target_lines.description: A hint for the drafting prompt: about how many spoken lines to write.

dialogue.table.description: The container and the output form.

doc.description: The dialogue container, by title or id.

includeConditions.description: Adds a condition column for choices. Defaults to false.

name.description: The skill’s name, exactly as the skills list shows it.

skill.read.description: One reference or text asset of a skill loaded in this turn.

path.description: The file’s path under references/ or assets/ inside the skill folder.

memory.read.description: The memory note to read, or nothing to list what the project keeps.

slug.description: The note’s slug, as the memory index and the list show it. Leave it out to list every note.

agent.delegate.description: The agent to hand the work to, and what to tell it.

agent.description: Which built-in agent: reader (read-only research) or general (reads, and may propose steps).

brief.description: Everything the agent needs, in plain words: it sees nothing of this conversation but the brief and the scope.

scope.description: Documents the agent starts from: titles or ids, at most 20. Omit it and the agent finds what it needs with its read tools.

items.description: One document: a title, or an id.

text.search.description: Search current project text locally, without a provider request.

query.description: Words to find, with optional quoted adjacent-token phrases. No stemming or fuzzy matching.

scope.description: Binder node ids; folders expand to their descendants. Omit for the whole project, including eligible codex.

fields.description: Fields to search; omit for all four.

limit.description: The most hits to return, default 8 and at most 25.

excludeAfter.description: A focus document id: omit later manuscript passages but keep research.

focus.description: A document id for before/focus/after labels only.

session.history.description: Earlier turns in the current role’s conversation, newest first.

before.description: Return only turns older than this turn id from a previous page.

limit.description: The most turns to return, from 1 to 50. Default 10.

timeline.read.description: Which part of the timeline to read, and how to arrange it. Every parameter is optional.

axis.description: The axis to read: 'story' (default), 'narrative' (reading order) or 'braid' (both).

groupBy.description: The lanes to read: 'none' (default, one row per scene), 'pov', 'character', 'mode', 'folder', 'location' or 'thread'.

scope.description: A folder or document: a title, or an id. Only the scenes under it are read. Leave it out for the whole manuscript.

findings.description: 'open' (default) attaches the open findings to their scenes; 'none' leaves them out.

target.description: Only pictures placed at this document or folder (a title or an id, a paragraph of it counting), or "project" for the project as a whole.

limit.description: At most this many pictures, default 25.

maxPx.description: The longest side to send, in pixels, at most 1568. Default 1568. Smaller is cheaper and shows less detail.

pictures.annotate.description: The pictures or placements to describe, and what to set on each.

items.description: One entry per picture or placement. At most 50 per call.
One picture (a_ id) or one placement (l_ id), and the fields to change. A field left out stays as it is.

id.description: A picture id (a_…), or a placement id (l_…) for a note.

caption.description: The caption, at most 2000 characters. An empty string clears it. Pictures only.

alt.description: The alt text, at most 500 characters: what the picture shows, for a reader who cannot see it. An empty string clears it. Pictures only.

decorative.description: True marks the picture as decoration with no alt text to read; false clears the mark. Pictures only.

tags.description: The picture’s tags, replacing its current ones, at most 32. An empty list clears them. Pictures only.

note.description: A placement’s note, at most 2000 characters. An empty string clears it. Placements only.

pictures.attach.description: The placements to make and the placements to remove.

items.description: One picture, and where it goes.

to.description: Where the picture goes: the project, a binder item, or one paragraph of a document.

doc.description: The document or folder: a title, or an id. An ambiguous title lists its candidates.

oneOf.description: One paragraph of a document, named by a quote from it.

doc.description: The document: a title, or an id.

anchor.description: A short quote from the paragraph, at most 200 characters, exactly as the document reads. It must fit one paragraph only.

role.description: What the placement is. A card is the one picture a binder item shows on its card. Default reference.

note.description: A note about this placement, at most 2000 characters.

detach.description: Placement ids (l_…) to remove, at most 50. The picture stays in the library.

pictures.import.description: The staged picture to save, and what to record about it.

stagingId.description: The staging id the app gave the picture, from a drop, a paste or a tool result. It cannot be made up, and it can be used once.

links.description: Where to place the picture once it is saved, at most 50.

items.description: One placement: the project, a binder item, or one paragraph of a document.

doc.description: The document or folder: a title, or an id. An ambiguous title lists its candidates.

oneOf.description: One paragraph of a document, named by a quote from it.

doc.description: The document: a title, or an id.

anchor.description: A short quote from the paragraph, at most 200 characters, exactly as the document reads. It must fit one paragraph only.

alt.description: The alt text, at most 500 characters.

label.description: A short label, at most 200 characters.

server.description: The tool server that returned it, for kind mcp.

tool.description: The tool that returned it, for kind mcp.

pictures.place.description: The picture, the document and the paragraph it goes beside.

doc.description: The prose document: a title, or an id.

anchor.description: A short quote from the paragraph the picture goes beside, at most 200 characters, exactly as the document reads. It must fit one paragraph only.

position.description: Before or after that paragraph. Default after.

size.description: How large it prints. Default full.

revision.description: The revision of the document you read the quote from, when you have one. The call is refused if the document has moved on.

pictures.transcribe.description: The handwritten pages to transcribe, and where the reviewed text goes.

assetIds.description: One to 100 picture ids (a_…), each page named once.

into.description: Where the reviewed pages go once approved: a new Research document, or searchable text on the picture records.

language.description: The language of the handwriting, overriding the project language. A hint only: the transcription never corrects the text to match it.

secondRead.description: A second read on another vision route, to highlight the word-level disagreements for review. Omit it for one read. The agent loop checks this route’s vision capability and runs it as its own pinned, budgeted model call; nothing is merged automatically.

profileId.description: The provider profile the second read runs on.

model.description: A model on that profile. Omit for the profile’s default.

comic.derive.description: The comic book to derive, and the script to derive from.

book.description: The comic book: a folder title, or its id. An ambiguous title lists its candidates.

script.description: The comic script to derive the pages from: a document title, or its id. Default: the script the book links. A book with no link gets this one linked, when no other book holds it.

comic.letter.description: The comic book and the page of it to letter from the book’s linked script.

book.description: The comic book: a folder title, or its id. An ambiguous title lists its candidates.

page.description: The page to letter: its title, or its id, among the book’s pages. An ambiguous title lists its candidates.

panel.description: Letter only this panel of the script page, counted from 1. Default: every panel of the page.

line.description: Letter only this lettering line of that panel, counted from 1. Needs panel.

comic.scriptFromPages.description: The comic book whose pages to write the script from.

book.description: The comic book: a folder title, or its id. An ambiguous title lists its candidates.

doc.description: The document: a title, or an id.

target_words.description: The length to aim for, in words.

mode.description: draft replaces an empty body; continue appends; rewrite_selection replaces the anchored range.

selection.description: A range in the body projection, captured from the editor selection.

to.description: End offset, exclusive. Greater than from.

exact.description: The text between from and to, 1 to 2000 characters.

capturedRevision.description: The document revision when the anchor was captured.

include_forward_outline.description: Include the synopses of the later scenes in the drafting context. Off by default; turn it on when the draft must lead into what follows.

scene.apply.description: The text you wrote, where it goes, and the brief it answers.

doc.description: The document of the brief: a title, or an id.

text.description: The text, at most 16384 characters: the prose (or Fountain) only, with no preamble.

mode.description: The mode of the brief. draft replaces an empty body; continue appends; rewrite_selection replaces the anchored range.

selection.description: A range in the body projection, captured from the editor selection.

to.description: End offset, exclusive. Greater than from.

exact.description: The text between from and to, 1 to 2000 characters.

capturedRevision.description: The document revision when the anchor was captured.

briefId.description: The briefId the brief returned. A brief expires after 30 minutes, or when the text it was made from changes.

dialogue.brief.description: The container, the brief, and where the draft goes.

doc.description: The dialogue container, by title or id.

instruction.description: The creative brief for the beats.

fromBeats.description: Knot or stitch ids to continue from. The draft goes after the last one. Omit to append at the end.

target_lines.description: A hint for the drafting prompt: about how many spoken lines to write.

dialogue.apply.description: The Ink you wrote, where it goes, and the brief it answers.

doc.description: The container of the brief, by title or id.

ink.description: The Ink, at most 16384 characters: the Ink only, with no commentary and no code fence.

fromBeats.description: The knot or stitch ids of the brief. The Ink goes after the last one. Omit to append at the end.

briefId.description: The briefId the brief returned. A brief expires after 30 minutes, or when the text it was made from changes.

notes.replace.description: The document, and the notes that replace its current notes.

doc.description: The document: a title, or an id. An ambiguous title lists its candidates.

notes.description: The new notes, in full, at most 50000 characters. An empty string clears the notes.

synopsis.set.description: The document or folder, and its new synopsis.

doc.description: The document or folder: a title, or an id. An ambiguous title lists its candidates.

synopsis.description: The synopsis, at most 2000 characters. An empty string clears it.

vocabulary.upsert.description: The vocabulary term to add or change.

id.description: The id of an existing term to rename or recolour. Leave it out to add a new term.

name.description: The term’s name, which must differ from every other term of that kind.

id.description: The id of a saved filter to change (q_ and ten characters). Leave it out to save a new filter.

name.description: The filter’s name, at most 60 characters.

root.description: Search only this root. Leave it out to search both.

criteria.description: What a node must match, every criterion given at once.

text.description: Words to find, case-insensitive, at most 200 characters.

textIn.description: Where text is searched. Leave it out for all three.

statusId.description: A status id from the project vocabulary.

labelId.description: A label id from the project vocabulary.

keywordsAll.description: Keywords the node must all carry.

keywordsAny.description: Keywords the node must carry at least one of.

minWords.description: At least this many words (a folder counts its subtree).

maxWords.description: At most this many words (a folder counts its subtree).

createdWithinDays.description: Created in the last this many days.

modifiedWithinDays.description: Changed in the last this many days.

id.description: The id of a goal to change (g_ and ten characters). Leave it out to set a new goal.

node.description: The manuscript, or a folder: a title, or an id.

metric.description: What is counted. Defaults to words.

kind.description: project (the default), or a weekly or monthly writing pace.

resetDay.description: Weekly: the weekday the week starts on, 0 (Sunday) to 6. Monthly: a day 1 to 28, or "last". A project goal takes none.

anyOf.description: A weekday 0 to 6, or a day of the month 1 to 28.

comparator.description: at-least for a drafting goal, at-most for a length cap, about for within 10 percent.

deadline.description: A date such as 2026-10-31. Leave it out for an open-ended goal.

archived.description: True to hide a completed or abandoned goal from the rail.

title.description: A few words naming the habit, at most 120 characters, on one line.

type.description: style (how the prose reads), preference (what the writer likes or avoids), process (how the writer works) or reference (where to look).

body.description: The note, at most 4000 characters. Lead with the rule in one line.

slug.description: The note’s slug, to update one by name. Leave it out to make one from the title.

expectedDigest.description: The digest memory.read gave for the note you are changing. Leave it out for a new note.

text.description: The whole new CAOTANG.md, at most 50000 characters.

expectedDigest.description: The digest memory.read gave for CAOTANG.md. Leave it out when the project has none.

timeline.edit.description: The timeline edits, applied together or not at all.

ops.description: The edits, in order, at most 200. Each is read against the project as the edits before it leave it.

oneOf.description: Change the timing declarations of one scene or folder.

nodeId.description: The scene or folder: the nodeId timeline.read returned, or its exact title.

patch.description: The scene fields to change. Give at least one.

dayOffset.description: The scene’s day as a whole number from day 0, negative before it.

durationDays.description: How many days the scene spans, zero or more.

timelineMode.description: How the scene sits in time. "linear" is the ordinary case and clears any other mode.

pov.description: The point-of-view character: a codex entry id or its exact name.

storyPart.description: The part of the story the scene or folder is in. A folder’s part holds for what is inside it, unless a scene names its own.

mainStory.description: true puts the scene or folder in the main story even inside a prologue or epilogue folder, replacing a part of its own; false clears that mark.

after_add.description: Scenes this one must come after: a title or an id each. They are added to the scene’s existing "after" list.

after_remove.description: Scenes to take off this scene’s "after" list: a title or an id each.

clear.description: Fields to remove from the scene, so it has no value of its own: dayOffset (undated), durationDays, pov, storyPart or mainStory (it inherits again).

oneOf.description: Move a scene or folder to a place in the binder. Moving one never moves another.

nodeId.description: The scene or folder to move: an id, or its exact title.

newParentId.description: The folder to move it into, or "manuscript": an id, or its exact title.

index.description: Its position among the new parent’s other children, counted from 0 without the moved node.

oneOf.description: Move the days of many dated scenes by the same amount, as one edit. Every scene named needs a day.

delta.description: Days to add to each day, negative for earlier. Not zero.

nodeIds.description: The dated scenes to move: an id or an exact title each.

label.description: A short name for the batch, shown on the card and in the activity list, at most 200 characters.
